utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. And please, call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, soon to be joined by Ann Sutherland, assisted by Ruth Karper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this exact explanation. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and Mr. John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you, good afternoon. I asked for starting without the presence of the witness on purpose. You know that the outcome on the negotiations probably on agreed facts on signature and so on was due yesterday or yesterday evening. And I really don't want to go into details and waste the time with these technical questions right now. What I want to know is whether or not the parties are prepared to have a 65 ter (i) meeting tomorrow, 10.00, to discuss these issues without wasting the time necessary for hearing the witnesses being, at present, in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That would be acceptable to us. Just to inform Your Honours regarding the timing of the witnesses for the rest of this week, the next witness, I asked the VW services to bring that witness by 3.30 today in case we get to that witness today, which I think there's a good chance of. But I don't anticipate that witness taking more than a day, and that is the only witness we have left this week. There are no other witnesses. We tried to get another short witness this week, and we were not able to do so. We have another witness coming over the weekend and would be available Monday to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I understand. My only point is that unfortunately, we have a lot of administrative issues which we, at any rate, have to do in the courtroom, as the admission into evidence, we have to go through the documents. That will take time enough. The point was to discuss other issues in this environment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. We would be prepared to meet at the Court's convenience either tomorrow or at any time to discuss the signature issues. We are still working and contemplating some of the issues that were raised in the fourth amended indictment and have not included that discussion either between counsel as well as between the client. We anticipate that we will conclude that in short order, and depending again how the witnesses go the balance of the week, we will endeavour to utilize that time to meet with the client and see if we can at least provide the Court and opposing counsel with some stipulated facts or agreed facts as revealed or reflected in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I understand correctly that it would be better from your point of view to meet on Friday morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Or Thursday. Either way is fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then let's have the 65 ter (i) meeting tomorrow morning, 10.00, in my office. And the point, why I raised the question of agreement or not agreement, did the parties meet on the question whether or not we have go into details of the rape committed against the witness now before us? And the Bench, I have to emphasise, the Bench would appreciate if the parties could agree on the fact that the person, our witness, was raped in the past, and therefore both parties omit to ask any further questions to that crime, only to that crime. But I fully understand if the Defence regards it necessary to contest it. Of course it's your right. It's only the question whether or not you could agree on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Quite frankly, I don't believe that we had actually discussed with the Office of the Prosecution this very issue, but I know that we generally contemplated, just so the Court knows, our strategy is not to contest this witness' factual description of the sexual assault and rapes that occurred as she has alleged. However, we do have questions not of particular or specificity with respect to the rape. We do have some follow-up questions on the issues, and I could share them with the Court. And I prefer to do that so you can tell me if I should ask them or not. So I'm not sure if I should ask you now. I can wait. It just goes to documenting the rape, whether it was documented. We also have a concern quite frankly as to the stab wound that was on the left shoulder. It goes solely to credibility of the witness. I made some observations that perhaps the Court didn't. Perhaps I'm wrong in the observations I made in connection with her prior statement earlier and her discussion saying she couldn't lift her arm, as an example. Again, I'm not arguing the credibility of this witness and the specific sexual assaults that occurred to me, but I may question at some time other aspects of her testimony, although it all depends on how the cross goes. So I may ask her about that and I did plan on asking her if she could raise her arm because at one point it seemed to me from the transcript that she stated she was unable to raise it. If that's unacceptable, I won't ask those questions. If it is, then I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The question is: Is this point relevant for the Prosecutor's office, whether or not this witness has got this injury or not and the consequences of this injury.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, in respect of the injury, she has -- I've seen the injury, and she is willing to show the Court or we can have a photograph taken of her shoulder, which will show the wound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can I recall --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to your question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I recall that we have before us a case against Dr. Stakic, and to be very frank, it shouldn't be, and as a case as felt as a case against the witness, for me, it's difficult to understand, first of all, why the Office of the Prosecutor and under which legal perspective the Prosecutor would insist on the one or other point regarded to this crime because it would be really an advantage that we -- if it would not be necessary to go into details of these committed crimes -- committed crime, which is evidently far, far away from the responsibility of Dr. Stakic, to be that concrete.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness's credibility is of concern to us. In relation to your other question, I would defer to lead counsel to answer your question in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Our response is that we don't plan to go into further details unless we need to follow up on the Defence questions. As my co-counsel stated, if the Defence is attacking her credibility, that is of concern to us. We believe she is credible. And if there's any insinuation she is not, it's only fair to her to put on all the evidence that indicates she is telling us the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, the Defence is not and has not taking the position that this witness is not credible on events she personally suffered through in 1992, nor would we make that proposition even with much less with the witness present, but definitely not even outside of her presence. But our point that there were other facts that she discusses and other facts that she gave on her August 24th, 2000, statement which I expect to have questions answered to, if permitted, and depending on how those answers go, and I'm just giving the Court the foresight, my last section in questioning, I anticipate it, again depending on how the answers are given, and I am confident that they will be truthful, then I won't go into the issue of her stab wound. But I will not at all go into the sexual assaults and the rape that she sustained, in that summer of 1992, nor do we have an interest in doing that. But to answer a question previously raised by the Court if I may, we cannot, however, stipulate to facts that do not come or go against our client, as reflected in the fourth amended complaint. I just don't want, in the future, and I know I'm speculating, for someone to cues this Defence team or this defendant or anybody else here, stipulating to facts. And Mr. Kuruzovic, or whoever the allegations are made against, didn't have an opportunity to address that. We just don't want it to go on the record as a stipulation by the Defence, but we do not attack, or will not, attack her credibility on those assaults.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can I just raise one separate brief matter regarding the 65 ter meeting tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, but first to conclude on this issue, I understand that the Defence will be precise and as sharp as they regard it necessary, but in the way that in the past will treat the person in the way that can be accepted, have no doubt about this. I would have preferred if the Office of the Prosecutor would have indicated that this incident is no longer at stake, because really we have to take care not to run out of proportion. We should be aware what it is for such a person to be here as a witness in a case, not as you mentioned as the alleged perpetrator, but in a case against Dr. Stakic, where a totally different emphasis lies. So I think it's not necessary to go into other details, but it shows the importance to come as soon as possible really to agreed facts, and also to ask the Prosecutor once again, in how far it's possible and we regard it as necessary to streamline the case as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just briefly, we do think that an incident like this, that the accused, Dr. Stakic, does share some responsibility for this. I don't think this is the time the Court wants to hear my argument regarding why that's so. But we very much do believe that the impunity of crimes by individuals against non-Serbs during this time period was the result of a policy. Regarding the other matter I just wanted to bring up briefly for consideration at the meeting, I wanted to ask the Bench to consider how you want to handle the 92 bis statements that are admitted. This could affect the time we use on Friday. Does the Chamber wish that these actually be read in open Court? I don't know, or is it simply enough to have them submitted, in writing, to the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's enough -- we expect the motion to be submitted, in writing, as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't mean the motion, but the Court has granted the 92 bises. I think we've already submitted the majority of the statements, and that's my only question was, because of the translation issue, did you want those actually to be read in open court, or do you want those simply to be submitted for translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's discuss this also tomorrow at the 65 ter (i) meeting. Thank you. Then the witness may be brought in, please. We go in closed session once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 7.06 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 6th day of June, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
